News.title: Murdered beauty queen’s husband ‘admits breastfeeding their baby from her dead body’ after ‘his jealous mum shot her’
News.content:
THE husband of a murdered beauty queen claims he tried to breastfeed their baby from her corpse after she was allegedly shot dead by her “jealous” mum-in-law.

A major manhunt has been launched for Erika Maria Herrera, 63, after she was seen in haunting footage approaching Carolina Flores Gomez, 27, with a gun.





Carolina, a former Miss Teen Universe, was shot dead in the face, neck and head on April 15 – with prosecutors saying her mother-in-law is the main suspect.

Her husband Alejandro has claimed he decided to stay at home and not immediately report the shooting because he wanted to feed their baby, according to local crime reporter Carlos Jimenez.

He said he tried to breastfeed the tot – as Carolina had been doing at the time – and then bathed it before calling his lawyers.

It was only until the next day that he decided to alert cops.

He also claimed he feared the baby could be taken into care by social services.

Carolina’s mum, Reyna Gómez Molina, has accused Alejandro of keeping the body at home and delaying his call to the police in order to give his own mother time to escape.



Investigators have not confirmed the claims.

Chilling footage from the day of Carolina’s death shows two women walking into a room before gunshots and screaming are heard.

Herrera was inside the home with her son – Carolina’s partner – at the time of the shooting in Polanco, Mexico City.



The mum-in-law fled after the alleged killing and remains on the run.

The shooting is said to have happened late Wednesday night – but was not reported until the following day, reports say.

Alejandro has not been arrested but is understood to be under investigation as he failed to report his wife’s death immediately.

In the harrowing video of Carolina’s death, the former pageant winner from Baja California can be seen walking to the back of her home wearing a white robe.

Several local outlets have reported Carolina was going to get her mother-in-law a drink of water at the time.



Herrera is then seen following her before several gunshots ring out.

The victim’s husband, Alejandro, walks into the frame just seconds later, carrying the couple’s baby.

“What was that?” he asks his mother in Spanish.

“What did you do, crazy?” an unidentified person’s voice is heard saying.

“Nothing,” his mum answers. “She made me angry.”



“What’s wrong with you? She’s my family,” Alejandro says, calmly.

His mum replies: “You’re mine and she stole you”.

Spanish media outlet Debate spoke to a close friend of Carolina, who said the victim had been hounded by her mother-in-law when she fell pregnant.

The friend said Carolina believed that Herrera “never liked her” and that she had “gotten worse” since the pregnancy.

It has also been suggested that a multimillion-pound inheritance could be behind the killing.



Carolina is believed to have received a large sum of money following the death of her father.

The high-profile killing has left the Mexican community reeling, sparking a wave of protests in Mexico‘s Baja California over the weekend.

Carolina was born in San Diego, was crowned Miss Teen Universe for Baja California in 2017, and picked up several local titles in her home city of Ensenada.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The police investigation into the shooting remains ongoing.

News.title: Historic pub rebrands after owners claim 400-year-old name is ‘insensitive’ as locals blast ‘woke’ gone mad
News.content:
'WOKE' WATCH Historic pub rebrands after owners claim 400-year-old name is ‘insensitive’ as locals blast ‘woke’ gone mad

A HISTORIC pub is changing its 400-year-old name as the new owners believe its current one is “insensitive” and “offensive”.

Local punters of the boozer near Ripon, North Yorkshire, have blasted the rebrand as “woke” gone mad.





Publicans Laura Davis and James Campbell are changing the name of the former coaching inn near Ripon Racecourse from the Black A Moor Inn to The Furlong and Farrow.

In a statement posted to Facebook, they explained their decision: “The name change is simply because in today’s era, some would feel the name a little insensitive due to its relations to the slave trade and European artistic trope from the sixteenth to the eighteen centuries.

“We want our venue to be inclusive to all and to carry no unwelcomed bad relations to racism.

“We totally respect the history behind it and we hope that the public will understand our reasonings for this in today’s modern era.

“Black-a-moor is an archaic, offensive term for a Black person, often labeled as a racial slur in modern dictionaries.

“Pubs with this name often face scrutiny for perpetuating historical racism. We obviously want no affiliation with this in 2026!”

They will also be restoring the pub exterior back to its original heritage, in line with the other buildings in the historic market town, before the reopening on May 15.

The term “Blackamoor” is an old English term for black people, particularly those of African descent.



The word dates back to the Elizabethan times, and while it was often used historically without bad intent, it is now widely considered offensive.

Several pubs with similar names have rebranded in recent years – The Black-a-Moor pub in Preston was renamed to The Lancaster Gate in December 2024.

Some locals slammed the decision to rename the North Yorkshire pub – commenter Tom Rafal said: “I’m a dyed in the wool lefty, and even I think this is pathetic wokeness.”

Another called the decision “more ‘woke’ nonsense” and “Political Correctness strikes again”.

“Shouldn’t change the name. Has been called black a moor a long time. Pubs are landmarks… traditional… shame to change a part of history for no significant reason,” user Nigel Dale said.



“Ridiculous decision. Doesn’t cause anyone offence what so ever.”

Jags Semi added: “Erasure of history in the name of political correctness. Nobody cares about the name of a pub that’s been there for hundreds of years.

“There are many pubs with the same name as it was a popular pub name 200 years ago.”

However, some commenters agreed with the choice, calling the new name “great” and saying they “can’t wait to visit”.

A local said: “What a lovely post, very honest and transparent as well as being respectful. Wishing you and your team well with the new venture, exciting times, cheers.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The new Furlong and Farrow defended their rebrand, commenting: “We feel it incorporates the beautiful racecourse and the farming land and agriculture it’s built on.

“Whilst we understand people’s views and concerns, the word ‘blackamoor’ ‘can be’ considered offensive and its usage has previously resulted in legal or professional consequences for businesses.”

News.title: Evil Scots mum GUILTY of killing newborn baby despite blaming toddler for grim death
News.content:
AN EVIL mum killed her newborn baby by inflicting horrific “car crash” like injuries – before blaming a toddler.

Nicole Blain, 30, was today convicted of murdering three-week-old Thea June Wilson.





The helpless tot was left with a fractured skull, brain damage and two broken ribs after the savage attack on July 14, 2023, at a flat in Greenock, Inverclyde.

A jury at the High Court in Glasgow saw through Blain’s lies after hearing how the infant suffered injuries usually only seen in a road traffic accident.

Heartless Blain, of Greenock, had claimed a toddler had snatched 19-day-old Thea from her crib before dropping her and causing injuries so severe they were compared to a high-speed car crash.

The court heard how the tiny tot’s head had likely been hit off “a hard floor…at least three separate times”.

READ MORE ON THE SCOTTISH HOTEL BLAZE Huge fire tears through popular hotel as firefighters battle inferno



Tragic Thea also suffered a spinal bleed, blunt force trauma and bleeding to the eyes.

In a video of a gender reveal for the tragic tot, the heartless mum can be seen reacting angrily after learning she was having a baby girl.

The footage shows Blain stabbing a balloon with a knife and pink confetti flutters out.



She then gives the camera the finger and storms out of the room.

We told previously how the brute mother sent text messages to the tot’s gran saying “I can’t cope. My head’s a mess. I’m scared she’s going to die.”



The court was shown text messages earlier this week that Blain had sent to her mother-in-law, Laura Wilson, pleading with the grandmother to take the tot “for a couple of weeks” because she was struggling to cope.

In one text, Blain said: “I can’t cope Laura. I’m scared something happens to her.”

In another text, she pleaded: “I’m not well enough to do this and be responsible for a baby so little.

“My head is a mess. I’m scared she is going to die. It’s horrible.”

Blain claimed she had gone for a nap on July 13 after putting Thea into her ‘Beside Me crib’ and woke up after hearing her neighbour at the door looking to borrow some salt.



She claims the toddler – who was also in the house at the time – had taken the baby from the crib, removed two blankets and her nappy and left her lying at the bedroom door, whilst she had slept through.

Blain told the court that when she heard the door knock, she got up and walked past her injured baby, who was lying naked on the floor beside the bedroom door.

Blain said she answered the door before coming back in the room, again walking past the baby on the floor, to check the crib and only then did she realise the child had been moved.

Prosecutor Alan Cameron KC said: “Thea sustained some very serious injuries, including fractures to her skull, damage to her brain, bleeding in her eyes, and however that came to be inflicted upon her, you never woke up until someone knocked on your front door?”

Blain replied: “Yes”.



Blain claimed she “just assumed” the toddler had dropped the baby, causing the injuries, but numerous medics gave evidence saying the extent of Thea’s injuries could not have been caused by “a simple fall”.

Judge Scott adjourned sentencing for reports but told Blain: “When I sentence you I will be passing a life sentence.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Blain sobbed and wailed “I’m not going to be alright” as she was led from the dock.

She will return to court next month

News.title: What does 86 mean? Ex-FBI director James Comey charged over ‘86 47′ seashells pic ‘threatening Trump’
News.content:
A SINGLE photo has led to former FBI director James Comey being indicted for a second time.

One of Trump’s biggest political enemies posted on Instagram and later deleted a beach photo of seashells arranged to read ’86 47′ in May 2025, with a simple caption: “Cool shell information on my beach walk”.





Republicans saw the post as a message of violence against Donald Trump, and Comey was later investigated by the Secret Service.

During a press conference on Tuesday, May 28, 2026, Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche said : “You are not allowed to threaten the President of the United States of America.”

But what is the hidden message behind the mysterious beach photo?

What does 86 mean?

The number 86 is a slang defined by the Merriam-Webster dictionary as an expression of disapproval.



Informally, it can mean “to reject”, “to ban”, “to refuse to serve” or “to remove”.

Restaurant staff may sometimes use the numbers to mark a menu item that is no longer available or a customer who’s had one too many and shouldn’t be served anymore.

The term is believed to have come from 1930s soda-counter slang for an item that was sold out.

The true original of the phrase is unknown, but according to Merriam-Webster’s research, it was created as a rhyming slang for nix, which means “to veto” or “to reject”.



What does 86 47 mean?

While the number 86 has more of a generic meaning on its own, 47 likely refers to Donald Trump himself because he is the 47th president of the United States.

The post quickly sparked outrage from Republicans and Trump administration officials.

Comey insisted he did not know what the numbers meant, but Trump has disputed that.

“I didn’t realise some folks associate those numbers with violence,” he said. “It never occurred to me, but I oppose violence of any kind, so I took the post down.”

Trump argued that “a child knows what that meant”.



In an interview for Fox News, the US president said: “That meant assassination, and it says it loud and clear.

“Now, he wasn’t very competent, but he was competent enough to know what that meant.”

The indictment comes just days after a gunman was charged with trying to assassinate Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner.

News.title: Keir has dodged sleaze probe, but he’s not out the woods yet – Rayner’s return & cabinet reshuffle on cards to save face
News.content:
SIR Keir Starmer may have swerved a sleaze investigation into the Peter Mandelson scandal – but not even his closest aides think he is out of the woods.

The furore engulfing the PM over his doomed pick for US ambassador will dog him for months to come.





Not least because we are still expecting the release of tens of thousands of private messages sent between the Labour peer and those at the top of government.

Labour insiders fear “death by a thousand texts” in which highly-embarrassing WhatsApps and emails are thrust into public viewing.

And once again MPs will be forced to defend a PM with which they are quickly losing patience – until that patience snaps.

In recent days the Mandelson scandal has been embroiled in process and procedure that few voters in the real world will bother to follow.



But underestimating the public anger would be a grave mistake given the big picture offence is damning: that Starmer appointed the mate of the world’s most notorious paedo Jeffrey Epstein into the most distinguished of diplomatic postings.

MPs need no reminding of this. They get an ear-bashing every time they knock on doors in the local election campaign.



The elections themselves are expected to be brutal for the PM, who could lose up to a thousand councillors to Reform and the Greens.

Labour is expected to lose power in Wales for the first time in history, while also face defeat in Scotland despite the SNP’s torrid time in charge.

Candidates put to the sword of the electorate will waste no time blaming Starmer for their eviction.

Grim scenes will await tired MPs on the morning of Friday 8 May, as councillors – perhaps good friends – they have known for years lose their jobs.

For a PM with little political credit left in the bank, that will present possibly the most dangerous moment of his premiership so far.



Starmer will likely try to strangle any mutiny at birth by springing into a “reset” of his leadership.

That could involve a Cabinet reshuffle that brings in party left-wingers who pose the biggest risk of staging an insurrection.

Angela Rayner is expected to be offered a return to nobble her ability to mount a leadership challenge.

But while tilting the balance of power further to the left may appease hardline backbenchers, it could alienate the wider public to see his popularity plunge even further.

This is the thought currently occupying more moderate MPs who fear the threat to Reform far more than the Greens in their seats.



While many are fed-up with Starmer, they see him as a better alternative than Rayner or Miliband in No10.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

One Labour MP tells me: “The biggest thing keeping him there is the real fear of Rayner or Miliband.

“That’s terrifying. And it’d be three years of that, which for a party would be irrecoverable”.

News.title: Three men ‘firebombed car and homes linked to Sir Keir Starmer after being offered cash by Russian called El Money’
News.content:
'ARSON' ATTACKS Three men ‘firebombed car and homes linked to Sir Keir Starmer after being offered cash by Russian called El Money’

THREE men firebombed a car and homes linked to Sir Keir Starmer after being offered cash by a Russian called “El Money”, a court heard.

Jurors heard Ukrainian national Roman Lavrynovych, 22, first set fire to a Toyota RAV4 in Kentish Town on May 8.





He then allegedly carried out an arson attack three nights later on a home in North London.

The Old Bailey heard Lavrynovych also firebombed another house occupied by the Prime Minister’s sister-in-law on May 12.

Romanian Stanislav Carpiuc, 27, and Ukrainian national Petro Pochynok, 35, allegedly conspired with Lavrynovych to set the fires.

Carpiuc is accused of recruiting Pochynok to help Lavrynovych with the first fire while he oversaw planning and received payment, the court heard.

The three men all deny conspiring along with others to damage property by fire between 1 April and 13 May, 2025.

Lavrynovych, an “aspiring model” and roofer, denies two counts of damaging property with intent to endanger life.



Prosecutor Duncan Atkinson KC said: “Lavrynovych had been offered payment to set the fires by a contact using the name or pseudonym ‘El Money’.

“El Money communicated in Russian, in contrast to the Ukrainian otherwise used by the defendants.

“Three fires in the same area within five days would be pretty unusual. However, three fires all involving property linked to the same person were beyond a coincidence.

“The RAV4 car had once belonged to the Prime Minister, Sir Keir Starmer.

“[One house] was managed by a company of which the Prime Minister had once been director and shareholder.



“The [second] house still belonged to the Prime Minister, and was occupied by his sister-in-law.”

Jurors heard the fire at the first home was clearly set deliberately after a “petroleum distillate like white spirit” was poured on to the front door and ignited.

Mr Atkinson said the fire “spread into the hallway of the premises, putting the lives of the occupants at risk”.

The court was told Pochynok and Carpiuc were initially traced through telephone contact with Lavrynovych.

Mr Atkinson said: “Later it became clear that Pochynok had been recruited by Carpiuc to help Lavrynovych with the first fire, while Carpiuc’s role was planning and receiving payment.



“Analysis of messages and other material recovered from telephones recovered from, and connected with, these defendants reveal communication between them before and during the relevant period.

“Lavrynovych had been offered payment to set the fires by a contact using the name or pseudonym El Money.

“Police recovered contact on the Telegram messaging app between Lavrynovych and EL Money, which showed that Lavrynovych had been recruited, instructed and promised with payment for the fires that he was told to start.

“Police also recovered contact on the Telegram messaging app between Carpiuc and EL Money.”

Carpiuc, Lavrynovych and Pochynok all deny conspiracy to damage property by fire.



Lavrynovych alone denies two counts of damaging property by fire, intending to endanger the lives of others.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He further denies two lesser counts of damaging property by fire being reckless as to whether lives would be endangered.

The trial continues.

News.title: Horror moment plane nosedives out of the sky and crashes into airport hangar killing two and leaving at least 11 injured
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a plane has crashed into an airport hangar tragically leaving two people dead and injuring at least 11 others.

The light aircraft smashed into a building at Parafield Airport in South Australia, immediately killing the pilot and a passenger.





A terrifying video captured the moment the small plane veered off course while attempting to land, before crashing and sparking a huge blaze.

Looking as though it was at first circling around, the aircraft can be seen taking a spine-chilling dip.

It continued straight down towards the ground, before disappearing behind an airport building.

Shocking footage, captured by Joshua Lee Swanell, shows the aftermath of the crash as flames ripped through the hangar.



The huge blaze sent thick, black smoke billowing into the air.

The airport was immediately shut to all air traffic as the huge blaze raged on.



“All I could hear was this plane kind of pitch,” Swannell said.

“The pitch that it took, you could hear it struggle then straight down.

“I just heard the crash, it just happened all so quick.”

Emergency services desperately rushed to the scene at 2.10pm on Wednesday afternoon.

A total of 11 ground crew inside the hangar at the time of the crash had sustained burns, according to 7NEWS.



They were all rushed to hospital for treatment.

Casualties were split between two hospitals due to the scale of the horrific accident.

Four of the injured victims were taken to Royal Adelaide Hospital while the other seven were treated at Lyell McEwin Hospital.

A large number of student pilots were among the injured evacuated from the scene.

It remains unknown how many people had been on the plane or how many people were inside the hangar at the time of the crash, ABC News reported.



“There are reports of injuries at the scene. There’s no confirmed numbers at this stage,” Senior Constable Matt Brown from South Australia Police said.

A spokesperson from Adelaide Airport said they were “aware of the serious incident at Parafield Airport”.

“Emergency services are in attendance,” they said.

“Parafield Airport has been closed to all air traffic. However, we are allowing returning aircraft to land.”

They said first responders were called to the scene at an “area near Kings Road following reports that a small plane had collided with a hangar as it was attempting to land”.



“The immediate area has been evacuated as emergency services deal with the incident.

“Please avoid the area if possible,” they added.

Residents nearby also reported seeing clouds of smoke from miles away.

Closer by, Swannell said within minutes of the crash, it was impossible to see anything.

“No flames, but just all black,” he said.



The thick black smoke has spread across nearby neighbourhoods, with Metropolitan Fire Service advising people to stay inside.

“If you or anyone in your care are having difficulty breathing, seek medical attention from your local GP,” an MFS advice update said.

“If your symptoms become severe, call 000,” it added.

Adelaide resident Ben told ABC radio he could see the smoke from his home.

“It looks like a large fire in an aeroplane hangar. I’ve seen multiple fire trucks going through — this is probably the fifth one now, and multiple emergency services heading out there,” he said.



“It’s pretty big.

“You could see the gable in the front doors of the hangar billowing out black smoke, just coming out.

“[I] couldn’t see flames but it was quite large — you could see some sort of fuel.”

The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) has spoken out, saying it had “commenced a transport safety investigation into the accident involving a twin-engined Diamond DA42 aircraft at Adelaide’s Parafield Airport on Wednesday afternoon”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The statement said the ATSB had “deployed a team of transport safety investigators” from Canberra and Brisbane, who “specialise in aircraft operations, maintenance and engineering, human factors and survival factors”.



“They will arrive on site on Thursday morning, and over coming days will conduct a range of evidence-gathering activities, including site and wreckage examination, and recovery of any aircraft components of interest for further examination at the ATSB’s technical facilities in Canberra.”

News.title: Horrifying moment knifeman stabs two Jewish men, 30s & 70s, before trying to slash cops in rampage as man, 45, arrested
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a knifeman stabbed two Jewish men before trying to slash cops in a street rampage.

Cops arrested a 45-year-old man on suspicion of attempted murder after the attack near a synagogue in Golders Green, North London, at 11.15am.





The two men, aged in their 30s and 70s, were rushed to hospital where they are in a stable condition.

It is understood the knifeman was spotted on a main road full of shops, where a local yelled out a warning to others.



Footage shows a suspect running towards a Jewish man and lunging at him with a knife.

It is understood he then turned onto a side street and stabbed the second man outside a synagogue nearby.



Footage shows the suspect walking casually towards a bus stop before suddenly pouncing on an older man putting on a kippah.

The man attacks the pedestrian, pushing him into a bus stop while stabbing him.

Terror cops are leading the investigation and working with the Metropolitan Police to determine if there are any links to terrorism.

Shomrim, a Jewish community security organisation, said they “immobilised the suspect with a vehicle”.

Sir Keir Starmer said “the antisemitic attack in Golders Green is utterly appalling”, adding “attacks on our Jewish community are attacks on Britain”.



London Mayor Sir Sadiq Khan slammed the “appalling” stabbings and said: “London’s Jewish community have been the target of a series of shocking antisemitic attacks.”

Cops said the suspect tried to stab officers but they weren’t hurt.

“We are aware of the significant distress and concern this incident is likely to cause in the face of a number of incidents in the local area.

“A suspect is in custody, and investigators are considering all possible motives.

“We are working to establish his nationality and background.”



It comes in the wake of a series of arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in north London, with cops ramping up patrols on the streets.

The stabbings unfolded just minutes away from where four Jewish ambulances were firebombed in March.

Tory Party leader Kemi Badenoch called on the government to treat the rise in antisemitic attacks as “a national emergency”.



Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis said “words of condemnation are no longer sufficient” and called for “meaningful action”.

Israel’s foreign ministry said Starmer’s statements are “no substitute for confronting the roots of antisemitism”.

It added “the UK Government can no longer claim this is under control”.

The Board of Deputies of British Jews added: “We are aware of a reported stabbing incident in Golders Green, with two injured. The police have apprehended a suspect.

“We are liaising with the CST, Government and police to understand what has happened and ensure a forceful response.”



Starmer has told MPs it is “deeply concerning” and promised “those responsible will be brought to justice”.

“There is now a police investigation and I think we all need to do everything we can to support that investigation and be absolutely clear in our determination to deal with any of these offences, the like of which we have seen too much recently.

He said: “The antisemitic attack in Golders Green is utterly appalling.

“Attacks on our Jewish community are attacks on Britain.”

Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy added that the Golders Green attack is “horrific”.



“No one should live in fear because of who they are.”

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: “My thoughts are with the victims of the abhorrent attack in Golders Green this morning, and the Jewish community.

“I’m grateful for the work of the community and the police in apprehending the suspect, and to the emergency services for their quick response.



“The suspect is now in custody and I’m being kept updated on the situation.”

Jewish charity the Community Security Trust added: “There has been a knife attack today in Golders Green. The suspect has been arrested.

“We would like to thank Shomrim, Hatzola and The Met Police for their swift response.

“We are working closely with the police and urge anyone with information to contact the police, Shomrim and CST immediately.”

The Sun reported yesterday how terror cops were investigating a suspected arson attack at a memorial just streets away from the attack.



Police received reports of the fire in Golders Green in the early hours of Monday.

The wall is near a Jewish Centre and shows Iranians killed while protesting against the country’s regime.

Earlier in the month, a synagogue in Kenton, north-west London, suffered smoke damage after it was targeted in an arson attack.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A “bottle filled with accelerant” is understood to have been thrown through one of the place of worship’s windows.

It marked the fourth arson attack carried out in the last month with an Iranian linked group claiming they are responsible for several of the terrifying incidents.



Cops probing four north-west London arson attacks Monday, March 23: The first attack targeted a volunteer-led ambulance service run by the Jewish community in Golders Green.

News.title: B&M's 'magical' £8 garden buy creates 'soothing' sounds by day and glows at night
News.content:
B&M's 'magical' £8 garden buy creates 'soothing' sounds by day and glows at night

Shoppers can get a 'magical' garden light that comes with a 'soothing' bonus feature

View 3 Images B&M shoppers can enjoy the two-in-one garden light and decoration this spring and summer (Image: Getty)

With the weather warming up and sunny skies taking over, plenty of people will be keen to make the most of the balmy conditions by spending time in their gardens. For anyone hoping to add 'soothing' ambience to their outdoor spaces by day and at night, B&M may have just what shoppers need.

‌



As part of its latest range of garden decorations and lights, the budget superstore is selling a 'magical' light that comes with a bonus feature, sure to delight people who enjoy 'relaxing' sounds. The store has a Solar Powered Hot Air Balloon Light in stock, which has a wind chime attached.

‌



The £8 item automatically turns on at dusk and emits a "realistic" amber flame effect. It is free to use as the LEDs run off the power of the sun's rays, meaning no wiring is required, and rechargeable batteries are included in the box.

‌



In the product description, B&M says the dual-use garden decoration is ideal for gardens, patios and other outdoor spaces, and comes to life after sunset. The full description reads: "During the day, this charming Solar Powered Hot Air Balloon with Wind Chime creates soothing ambient tones in the breeze."

It adds: "As the sun sets, it comes to life with a warm glow from the realistic flame effect LEDs, adding a magical touch to any outdoor space." The hot air balloon light is made with "premium" glass and features an ombre effect of red, orange, and green.

View 3 Images Solar Powered Hot Air Balloon with Wind Chime (Image: B&M)

‌



Shoppers can browse more of B&M's Decorative Solar Garden Lights online and in stores. Elsewhere, B&Q is selling a similar version of the wind chime light for a higher price.

The DIY high street store is selling the Lunaria Hanging Solar Hot Air Balloon Wind Chime for £26.99. Similar to B&M's option, it comes with a wind chime and an ombre-effect hot air balloon.

However, by opting for B&M's £8 version, shoppers can save almost £20. In the product description, B&Q says: "A distinctive hanging feature that combines gentle movement, soft sound and ambient light. Designed in a hot air balloon form, this piece creates a soothing chime in the breeze while emitting a warm, flame-like glow after dark."

‌



View 3 Images B&Q's similar Lunaria Hanging Solar Hot Air Balloon Wind Chime is available for £26.99 (Image: B&Q)

In other B&M news, shoppers can add a touch of "exotic elegance" in their gardens this season thanks to a set of 'Moroccan' lights. The store is selling a pack of two Solar Powered Morocco Wall Lights for £7.

The solar-powered wall lights run on sunlight, so they won't add to your electricity bills. They also come with rechargeable batteries and feature a "realistic amber flame effect".

Article continues below

In the full product description, B&M says: "Add a touch of exotic elegance to your outdoor space with this pair of Solar Powered Morocco Wall Lights." It adds: "With flame effect LEDs and beautifully intricate Moroccan-inspired patterns, these wall light cast stunning decorative light effects that enhance any patios, gardens, balconies, and pathways."

News.title: Wes Streeting warns of long-term effects of vaping as he vows crackdown
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Wes Streeting warns of long-term effects of vaping as he vows crackdown

Health Secretary Wes Streeting tells vapers ‘learn the lessons of previous generations and don’t make the same mistakes your parents and grandparents did’ with smoking

View 3 Images Vaping is a recent phenomenon so long term health impacts are largely unknown (Image: Getty Images)

Wes Streeting has promised a crackdown on how vapes are promoted in shops to tackle “an explosion in youth vaping”.

‌



The Health Secretary says the government will use new powers granted under the historic Tobacco and Vapes Act - which has become law today - to clamp down on advertising and promotion of e-cigarettes in shops up and down the country. Adverts, billboards and sponsorship by vaping companies will be outlawed.

‌



The Government also plans a consultation on whether vapes should be in plane packaging and hidden from display under the counter - the same as cigarettes.

‌



Mr Streeting told the Mirror: “From next summer, the days of flashy vape ads and sponsorships will be over. Tough new rules will shut down advertising that all too often targets children.

View 3 Images Brightly coloured vapes display in shop (Image: Getty Images)

BREAKING: New Tobacco and Vapes law to see UK become first country to end smoking READ MORE :

“Let’s be clear: vaping should only ever be used to help adults give up smoking but never, in any circumstances, by children. Unfortunately, we’ve seen an explosion in youth vaping with rates more than doubling in five years. One in four kids have now tried it, no doubt enticed by bright packaging, sweet flavours and aggressive promotion.”

‌



The Government confirmed today that implementation will take place from June 1 next year to give industry at least one year’s notice. It will drastically reduce the prominence of brightly coloured e-cigarette advertising in corner shops while vending machines selling vapes will also be banned.

The new law provides powers to regulate the flavours, packaging and display of all vapes and other nicotine products. It will stop them being targeted at children with bright colours and fruit flavours.

The clampdown will close loopholes to ban all vapes and nicotine products from being sold to under 18s - including nicotine pouches. Free “taster” products will also be banned.

‌



Wes Streeting added: “We’re closing the loopholes. No sales to under-18s. No free samples. No vending machines. No ifs. No buts. We’re also consulting on introducing vape-free spaces: from playgrounds to schools, and indoor public places. And we will be consulting on proposed restrictions around the shop display, packaging and appearance of vapes later this year.

View 3 Images Wes is warning of potential vaping harms (Image: PA)

“Emerging evidence already suggests young vapers are almost as likely to suffer shortness of breath, wheezing and chest pain as young smokers. Vapour can contain nicotine and other potentially toxic substances.

‌



“And while we do not know the long-term effects of many vape ingredients or the harms inhaling the contents and flavouring of vapes, given their widespread use is relatively recent, the expert advice is clear they are unlikely to be beneficial.

“It is possible further harms will emerge over time and my advice to young vapers and parents is why take the risk. Learn the lessons of previous generations and don’t make the same mistakes your parents and grandparents did.”

The link between tobacco smoking and cancer was uncovered in the 1950s but it took decades for attitudes to change and for smoking rates to fall steadily. Some 5.3 million people still smoke but this number has been overtaken by the numbers vaping.

Article continues below

The NHS still promotes e-cigarettes as a quitting aid for smokers but there are concerns about the number of young people taking up vaping who have never smoked. Research from recent years suggests vaping harms are much less than smoking.

News.title: Nigel Farage 'must face probe over £5m donation from crypto billionaire' demand
News.content:
Nigel Farage 'must face probe over £5m donation from crypto billionaire' demand

Nigel Farage reportedly received a £5million donation from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne shortly before entering Parliament, but did not declare it - saying the cash pays for his security

View 3 Images Nigel Farage faces questions over a £5million donation which he says pays for his security

Nigel Farage should face a standards probe after failing to declare a £5million donation from a crypto billionaire, critics have demanded.

‌



The Reform leader has come under fire after it emerged he had been given the sum by Thailand-based tycoon Christopher Harborne shortly before becoming an MP. Parliamentary rules state that new MPs have to declare donations and gifts in the year before they enter Parliament.

‌



Mr Farage has claimed the seven-figure sum was given to him to pay for his security. Mr Harborne made the donation before he announced he was standing in Clacton, The Guardian reports.

‌



Before the newspaper published the claim, Mr Farage gave an interview with The Telegraph saying his home had been firebombed. He claimed the billionaire's cash was being used to protect him - alleging the Home Office had turned down his requests for security.

Nigel Farage reveals home was firebombed - and billionaire funds his security READ MORE :

Minister lashes out at Labour rebels after tense vote over Starmer probe demand READ MORE :

View 3 Images Christopher Harborne, who is also known by the Thai name Chakrit Sakunkrit, is one of the biggest donors in British political history (Image: Linedin)

Tory chairman Kevin Hollinrake responded: "As a new Member of Parliament, Mr Farage was obliged to report to the House of Commons all political donations and political gifts he had received during the previous 12 months.

‌



"The Conservatives are today referring Nigel Farage to the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner. This £5 million from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne raises serious questions.

"What is Nigel Farage hiding? And why does Reform think the rules don’t apply to them? This stinks and Reform should come clean now."

And Labour's Anna Turley said: “Nigel Farage appears to have broken the rules again by failing to declare this cash from his billionaire backer."

‌



She added: "It’s simply not good enough for Reform to gloss over these egregious acts and further erode public trust in politics. It’s just the latest alarming example of Farage and his MPs believing there is one rule for them and another for everyone else.”

View 3 Images Mr Farage was hit by a milkshake while he campaigned in 2019 (Image: Getty Images)

Mr Harborne - who also goes by the name Chakrit Sakunkrit in Thailand - has donated £22million to Mr Farage's party since 2019, as well as £1.6million to the Tories. At the time of the donation to Mr Farage in 2024, he had said he had no intention of standing to be an MP.

‌



The £5million donation does not appear in the members' register of interests. But Reform claims it is confident rules have been followed.

Mr Farage leader told The Telegraph: “This money was given to me so that I would be safe and secure for the rest of my life.

“I have tried and failed in the past to get security funded by the Home Office and I don’t think the state will ever help me. I’m very much on my own and will be for the rest of my life, and I have to face up to that grim reality. Christopher is an ardent supporter who is deeply concerned for my safety. “I would rather not be discussing any of this but I am having to because someone has got hold of material about my private finances, which is outrageous, and which I believe was illegally obtained.”

‌



He said his home had been firebombed early last year and said he regularly faces threats to his safety. Mr Farage - who had milkshakes and a rock thrown at him during the General Election campaign in 2024 - said he has also previously had to write off a car after protestors attacked it.

Mr Harborne has a 12% shareholding in crypocurrency Tether. The billionaire was with Mr Farage when he had milkshake thrown at him while campaigning in Newcastle in 2019, The Telegraph reported.

It comes amid calls to cut the amount political donors are allowed to give. Harry Quilter-Pinner, executive director of think-tank the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR), said: “It’s becoming harder to ignore the growing weight that extremely wealthy donors appear to carry in British politics, not just in scale, but in proximity to key political decisions.

‌



“Reports that Christopher Harborne provided Nigel Farage with £5 million shortly before his change of stance on standing as an MP will inevitably prompt questions about influence, perception, and the standards we expect in public life.

“Seven-figure sums entering politics were once exceptional, now they are commonplace. The government must act urgently, capping individual donations at £100,000, to protect the sanctity of our politics.”

A Reform spokesman said: “This was a personal unconditional gift that was given before he was elected. We are confident everything has been declared in accordance with the rules.”

Article continues below

The MPs' code of conduct insists that donations in the year before entering the Commons should be declared. It states: "New Members must register all their current financial interests, and any registrable benefits (other than earnings) received in the 12 months before their election within one month of their election, and Members must register any change in those registrable interests within 28 days."

News.title: New tobacco and vaping law to see UK become first country to end smoking
News.content:
New tobacco and vaping law to see UK become first country to end smoking

Tobacco and Vapes Act receives royal assent to begin Britain’s phase out of the legal sale of tobacco products to children born on or after 1 January 2009

View 3 Images Stub it out - new law to end tobacco sales to future generations (Image: PA)

A historic legal change to phase out the sale of cigarettes has become law in the UK today.

The Tobacco and Vapes Act includes a landmark phase out of the legal sale of tobacco products to children born on or after 1 January 2009. As the bill gained Royal Assent, research published by Cancer Research UK estimated that it will mean 13 million children alive today will never be legally sold tobacco in the UK.

The charity said that if the legislation has the impact the government hopes then by 2040, up to 10 million fewer cigarettes will be smoked each day in the UK.

It makes Britain the first major nation to outlaw the sale of tobacco products to future generations.

View 3 Images Over five million Brits still smoke (Image: PA)

Smoking and vaping to be BANNED in these public areas - changes in full READ MORE :

Michelle Mitchell, chief executive officer at Cancer Research UK, said: “This is a truly historic achievement that will help to save and improve lives. With the new law in place, we are moving towards a future where children will grow up shielded from the lifelong harms of tobacco.

“It will mean more people living a life free from the grip of deadly addiction, fewer people facing a cancer diagnosis and less pressure on an already over stretched health service."

The UK is the first large country to implement the phasing out of the sale of tobacco products. The Maldives did so last year following similar legislation in New Zealand although the latter was later repealed.

View 3 Images The new law to phase out smoking has been dubbed 'world leading' (Image: Unknown)

An estimated 800,000 people in the UK have lost their lives to diseases caused by tobacco smoking in the last decade. Every year smoking leads to over 400,000 hospital admissions in England, costing the NHS £1.8 billion a year.

Action on Smoking and Health (ASH) estimates that smoking costs the economy £27.6 billion each year. Around 5.3 million people in the UK still smoke.

The bill was first introduced under the previous Conservative government and developed and carried forward by the current Labour government. Recent polling by Cancer Research UK found that 72% of people support raising the age of sale of tobacco products gradually to prevent future generations from ever legally being sold tobacco.

Ms Mitchell added: “Today’s milestone is the result of decades of research, overwhelming support in Parliament, tireless campaigning and backing from people whose lives have been devastated by smoking.

"Governments across the UK must now ensure the Act is implemented fully in every nation, alongside support to help people quit smoking. A future free from the lethal harms of tobacco is firmly within reach.”

England top cop is on a quest to find the next 'Lioness'

News.title: Donald Trump makes very awkward joke to Melania about marriage
News.content:
Donald Trump makes very awkward joke to Melania about marriage

US president Donald Trump, 79, told 56-year-old Melania 'it's not going to work out' in a joke about their marriage during King Charles' visit to the White House

Donald Trump comments on his marriage longevity during King visit speech

Donald Trump joked about how long he and Melania will be married in a revealing moment during the King's state visit.

‌



Just days earlier, Trump had called for late night TV host Jimmy Kimmel to lose his job after he made a joke about Melania being an "expectant widow" - a comment that came before the failed assassination attempt at the White House Correspondent's gala.

‌



But the US president made a very similar gag in front of King Charles, Queen Camilla and guests on the South Lawn yesterday as he reflected on his father Fred's 63-year marriage to his mother, Mary Anne.

‌



Trump looked over at Melania briefly as he said: "That's a record we won't be able to match, darling.

King Charles US visit live: Trump posts chilling Iran threat hours after state dinner READ MORE :

"I'm sorry, it’s just not going to work out that way. We'll do well, but we're not going to do that well."

‌



It was one of a number of jokes made by both Trump and the King throughout the day, as both sides put on a good-humoured display following the recent political rows over the Iran war.

Referring to the upcoming 250th anniversary of US independence from Great Britain on July 4, the King assured Congress that he was “not here as part of some cunning rearguard action”, which drew a laugh from some members of Congress.

"She really did love the family but I also remember her saying very clearly, ‘Charles, look young Charles, he’s so cute’. My mother had a crush on Charles. Can you believe it, amazing how… I wonder what she’s thinking right now?"

News.title: Mum thought £1million William Hill jackpot win was a gift from 'beyond the grave'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Mum thought £1million William Hill jackpot win was a gift from 'beyond the grave'

Claire Ainsley thought a win of more than £2million was a gift sent from her late mum... but instead it was an error made by betting agent William Hill after a technical error

View 5 Images Claire Ainsley cried tears of joy and thanked her mum after she thought she'd won more than a million (Image: Supplied)

A mum told how she thought her million-pound jackpot win was a “miracle from beyond the grave”, but instead of a “gift” from her late mum, Claire Ainsley, 27, received a message from William Hill stating it had been an error.

‌



“It’s been a nightmare. My mum recently died as well and she was only 45 and I thought it was a gift,” said Claire, who has a six-year-old son and a seven-year-old daughter.

‌



“Every single day before they go to bed my daughter Skylar and son Logan say ‘goodnight twinkle star nanna.’ So I thought it was a miracle.”

‌



Her mum, Lisa, died of Crohn’s disease two years ago and Claire wanted to give some money to their charity to help other sufferers. The single mum thought Lisa was the reason she came up as a £1million winner while playing the Jackpot Drop game on the William Hill app.

But she later received an email stating the win was the result of a technical error and that she would not receive a penny. She is now fighting for the prize she was promised.

“It’s been terrible and so stressful. I thought we would be able to live a better life and get a bigger house for us,” she said.

‌



View 5 Images Claire with her son Logan and daughter Skylar who she had to tell they were not milionaires afterall (Image: Supplied)

William Hill customers see dreams shattered after being hit by gambling 'glitch' READ MORE :

“I told my daughter and family and she was so happy. But then I had to tell her I didn’t win and she got upset and I got upset too. I told her ‘the game didn’t work properly so mummy didn’t get the money’.

Claire from Boroughbridge in North Yorkshire, explained how she put £14 on her account and was doing £1 bets at a time “when the jackpot came down”.

‌



“I could not believe it at the time and went back off it three times. I felt like I was going to have a heart attack, I couldn't breathe, I was crying with joy in the kitchen and saying 'thank you to my mum'. I was telling her I'd look after her grand-babies even more. She loved them so much. My kids really miss her."

The mum said she was even getting more money after the £1.27m: "I was then getting £20, £30 and it was going up like that. It's all still there now, it's so annoying.”

View 5 Images Lisa Ainsley, who died two years ago. (Image: Supplied)

‌



The mum says she even messaged William Hill and they confirmed it would be in her bank in 72 hours. “I screenshotted it all and it was declined after three days. I was gutted and heartbroken. Then telling my children made me feel so guilty. Their faces were so sad and disappointed.

“We had so many plans, my kids have never been on holiday abroad as I’m a single mum. I was going to take them to Spain and get passports. I was going to get them a house when they get older so I knew they would be stable and looked after for life. I’m just so gutted.

5 View 5 Images Claire thanked her mum Lisa Ainsley for her win only to be left 'heartbroken' again (Image: Supplied) 5 View 5 Images Skylar and Logan were excited about going on their first holiday abroad (Image: Supplied)

‌



“My mental health has got a lot worse because of all this. It’s been really depressing and so frustrating, I log on and look on my account and the proof is all still there. They are just ignoring me now.”

She claimed at one stage they offered her £34, but said: “It’s not good enough and that would not even buy one passport!” Claire revealed that this has not only happened to her but also to multiple other people in a Facebook group she is in.

The Mirror has previously told how one grandad had a heart attack after struggling to withdraw the money after a big win of more than £275,000 and desperately trying to get hold of William Hill only to be told later it was a ‘glitch’.

Article continues below

An Evoke spokesperson said: “During a routine review of platform activity, we identified an issue affecting the Jackpot Drop game which temporarily resulted in incorrect sums being credited to players’ balances and withdrawals being processed incorrectly.

“Whilst we quickly identified and resolved this issue, for a short period of time funds were erroneously credited to some customer accounts that were not correctly generated through valid or properly functioning gameplay.

“We have contacted relevant customers to clarify the issue, and are in the process of retrieving the funds in line with our standard terms and conditions. We have been grateful for our customers’ understanding on this matter and apologise for the inconvenience caused.” They refused to confirm how many customers were affected by the issue.

News.title: How Golders Green became a home for the UK’s Jewish community as Starmer condemns attacks
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

This article was originally published on 25 March 2026 and is being republished after a Jewish security group reported a man has been arrested after two people were stabbed in Golders Green.

The arson attack on four ambulances in Golders Green early on 23 March has been called “a horrific antisemitic attack” by the prime minister, Keir Starmer.

These ambulances were run for the benefit of both the local Jewish and non-Jewish communities in this district of north London by a charity called Hatzola (“rescue” in Hebrew). As these ambulances played a key supportive role in enabling access to health provisions for the good of all, it is especially shocking – and has further heightened the anxieties of British Jews.

This is a community still reeling after the attack on the Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester in October 2025 on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish religious calendar, which killed two people.

And the arson attack is part of a wider international wave of antisemitism, which has included Norway, the US and the Netherlands in the past few weeks. This is not an easy time to be a diaspora Jew.

Those who have carried out the attacks have come from different backgrounds. Many have been influenced by online hate emanating from Isis, and potentially individuals or groups supportive of the hardline Iranian regime.

Counterterror police are investigating whether an Iran-linked group is responsible for the arson. The terror group, Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (The Islamic Movement of the People of the Right Hand), has claimed responsibility for the attack, as well as others in Europe.

open image in gallery Gas canisters kept in the ambulances exploded in the conflagration ( PA Wire )

These attacks reflect the complex pattern of hostility towards Jews in the UK, which has been through a mixture of domestic and foreign-inspired hatred. In terms of the latter, there are several examples going back a century that can be highlighted.

The most well-known is the Jew hatred spread by Oswald Mosley and his British Union of Fascists (BUF), formed in 1932, which was at least partly stimulated by German Nazism.

Overall, however, there are deep domestic roots of antisemitism since the readmission of the Jews to England in the 17th century after a more than 300-year expulsion. But it has rarely resulted in violent attacks – even if it has made life uncomfortable for the Jewish minority in moments of crisis.

Golders Green’s rich history

These roots can be seen in relation to Golders Green, which started to develop as an area of Jewish settlement from the First World War onward. While there were some Jews in the then small suburb in the 19th century, there was not much in the way of a formal community.

Author Pam Fox, who has written the social history of Golders Green’s Jewish community, said: “Before 1910 there was just a handful of Jews living in the community, but by 1915 … there were 300 households”. Growth continued after the First World War, and in 1922 the first synagogue, Dunstan Road, was opened. Today, the Jewish population is around 8,000 and represents some 40 per cent of the suburb’s population.

Such crude statistics do not reflect the diversity of the Jewish population both past and present. As early as the 1930s, more orthodox Jews, some of them refugees from Nazism, were establishing different forms of worship to Dunstan Road, which was more in the form of mainstream orthodox religiosity. By the Second World War, there were at least 14,000 Jewish refugees in northwest London (including Golders Green), who varied from the totally secular, to reformers, to the ultra orthodox.

open image in gallery Local residents walk past a cordoned-off area as police investigate the stabbing of two people in the Golders Green neighbourhood of northwest London on 29 April 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

After the war, there were further influxes of Jewish refugees, including from Egypt, Hungary and later South Africa, as well as second- and third-generation Jews whose origins were from eastern Europe and then the East End of London. While the very orthodox are currently the growing group in Golders Green, it still has an incredibly heterogeneous Jewish population.

For most Jews, the vibrant cultural, social and religious life of Golders Green has made it a very comfortable place to call home. Even so, there has been antisemitism – organised in the form of the BUF and more commonly in the form of casual prejudice.

In late 1945, the Hampstead Petition Movement aimed to remove all foreign Jews from the wider area, and it had some local support. In the Nazi era, local newspapers, including the now defunct Golders Green Times, objected to the alleged bad behaviour of the Jewish refugees who were falsely accused of being unpatriotic and selfish.

About the author Tony Kushner is a James Parkes Professor of Jewish/non-Jewish Relations at the University of Southampton. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Today, the idea of Golders Green being a Jewish suburb ignores the reality that most of its population does not have that background. It also forgets the many types of Jewishness that are articulated there. Such nuances are lost on those carrying out the attack on the ambulances, with their universal usage.

It says much about the times that such distinctions are not made – many people hold all Jews responsible for the actions of a particular Israeli government. Yet in Golders Green as elsewhere, Jews for both political, cultural and religious reasons hold a range of attitudes towards the problems of the Middle East. Ultimately, such attacks are, as local Jewish resident Sam Adler put it, “cynical and cowardly”. If nothing else, as with Manchester, they have also brought communities together in solidarity and resistance to the ugliness of antisemitism.

Former Chicago White Sox star Alexei Ramirez has been provisionally banned from baseball after testing positive for four anabolic steroids during the World Baseball Classic in March, where he made headlines as the tournament's oldest ever player.

The International Testing Agency (ITA) confirmed on Wednesday that the 44-year-old Cuban tested positive for "metabolites of mesterolone, metandienone, oxandrolone and stanozolol."

These substances, the Lausanne-based agency noted, are "associated with promoting rapid muscle growth, increased strength and enhanced physical performance."

The ITA informed Ramirez of the positive result from a sample taken during the tournament.

Ramirez had returned to the Cuba roster after a 20-year absence, featuring as a bench player to break the record previously held by Roger Clemens, who was 43 when he represented the United States in the 2006 WBC.

open image in gallery Ramirez broke the record previously held by Roger Clemens ( Getty )

Cuba failed to advance from the pool phase in the recent tournament.

Known for his nine-year career in Major League Baseball, Ramirez spent seven years at the Chicago White Sox between 2008 and 2015.

He was the runner-up for the American League Rookie of the Year award in 2008 after making his debut earlier that year at the age of 26.

He also played in the Major League Baseball All-Star Game in 2014 and won the Silver Slugger Award twice in 2010 and 2014.

Ramirez went on to have short spells at the San Diego Padres and the Tampa Bay Rays in 2016 before walking away from Major League Baseball.

He also boasts an Olympic gold medal with Cuba from the 2004 Athens Games and won the Baseball World Cup the following year in Rotterdam, Netherlands, before being part of a silver medal-winning team at the 2006 World Baseball Classic in San Diego, California.

During his MLB tenure through 2016, he hit 115 home runs and recorded 590 RBIs.

News.content:
Police appear to arrest man after two people stabbed in Golders Green

Specialist officers from counter-terrorism policing are investigating after two men were stabbed in a Jewish area of north London.

A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after the attack Golders Green, the Metropolitan Police said.

The suspect was Tasered after he allegedly tried to stab police officers.

Jewish neighbourhood watch group Shomrim said a man was seen running along Golders Green Road armed with a knife and “attempting to stab Jewish members of the public”.

He was reportedly detained by members of the public before police arrested him. The two people stabbed were taken to hospital and were in a stable condition, the Met said. Jewish ambulance service Hatzola also took one person to hospital.

Prime minister Sir Keir Starmer condemned the “utterly appalling” attack and vowed that “those responsible will be brought to justice”.

Jewish charity the Community Security Trust (CST) said it was working closely with the police and urged anyone with information to contact the police, Shomrim and CST immediately.

The incident took place not far from where four Hatzola ambulances were set on fire in an antisemitic hate crime on Highfield Road in April. There has been a string of arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in north London.

News.title: King Charles’ standout jokes as he charms room in state banquet speech
News.content:
King Charles cracked jokes as he attended a formal state dinner with Donald Trump as part of his US visit on Tuesday (28 April).

The historic state trip, the King’s first to the US as monarch and the first state visit of any British monarch since 2007, marks the 250th anniversary of American independence.

Raising a toast during the state banquet, His Majesty joked that the lavish event was “a very considerable improvement on the Boston Tea Party”, referencing the 1773 protest which preceded the American Revolution.

From making light-hearted jabs at Mr Trump’s new White House East Wing ballroom project, to joking that the US should be thanking the UK that they aren’t speaking French, his speech left attendees in fits of giggles.

The chief executive of Bristol Bears has said that the Gallagher Prem side factors off-field profile into discussions over player recruitment, describing the club as “a marketing agency that plays rugby”.

Tom Tainton was appointed as CEO at Ashton Gate last summer having previously served as the club’s chief operating officer and head of communications.

The club sit fifth in the Prem table as they chase a play-off place this season, and have made a number of eye-catching additions to their playing group over the last few seasons.

Wales international Louis Rees-Zammit returned to rugby from the NFL last summer at the club and has since signed a long-term deal, while Ilona Maher’s short stint in Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR) last season drove significant interest both in the Bears and the league as a whole.

Tainton cited both as examples of how rugby can market its stars, and said that Bristol consider marketability when contemplating new signings.

“There is no point going to market and spending marquee money on a player and just expect them to do something between the white lines on a Saturday,” Tainton explained at SportPro London.

“In the grand scheme of things, nobody remembers how Bristol got on against Harlequins two years ago. They will remember how a player made them feel.

open image in gallery Ilona Maher's short stint at Bristol proved impactful for the PWR as a whole ( Getty )

“At Bristol Bears, we don’t call ourselves a rugby club. We are a marketing agency that plays rugby. Yes, our players have to be competent and able to deliver on the field, but if they are not bringing any value off the field, that genuinely factors into our recruitment conversations."

Tainton’s comments come with the Prem moving towards an expansion model having removed promotion and relegation, and amid fresh investment within English rugby.

Red Bull bought Newcastle last summer while James Dyson has recently purchased a 50 per cent stake in Bath, with the billionaire owners of AFC Bournemouth also expected to soon complete a takeover of Exeter Chiefs.

Bristol have been owned by Steve Lansdown since 2008, and Tainton suggested they are fully bought in to the Prem’s vision for the future.

open image in gallery Bristol recently took on Harlequins at Cardiff's Principality Stadium ( Getty )

“It is very easy for us to sit here and use a lot of corporate buzzwords that don’t really mean anything,” he stressed. “You want someone to see a sport that is cool, inclusive, engaging, and high-octane.

“I’d argue we have done the hard bit – the product is superb. There are young, articulate men and women playing the game. We’ve got a great base to grow from. We now have to take some bold risks to get out of our comfort zone and do things that the sport hasn’t previously done."

Embattled Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will be in the hot seat Wednesday morning, where he is set to face a grilling from lawmakers about his handling of the Iran war for the first time since the conflict began.

Hegseth is due to be questioned under oath by the House Armed Services Committee alongside Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, as negotiations to end President Donald Trump’s war remain at an impasse.

Trump aired his frustrations on Truth Social Wednesday, with an AI-generated image of himself holding a gun against the backdrop of explosions in Iran.

The war, which Hegseth pledged in early March would likely last between “four to five weeks,” has now entered its eighth week.

Democratic Rep. Jason Crow of Colorado, who sits on the committee, told Politico that “Hegseth’s got a lot to answer to from this disastrous war,” while fellow Democrat Rep. Chris Deluzio of Pennsylvania accused the Pentagon chief of “dodging congressional questions about the Iran war since Day One.”

Hegseth will also likely be questioned about his hollowing out of leadership at the Pentagon after he fired Navy Secretary John Phelan and the chief of staff of the Army, Gen. Randy George.

Trump fired Kristi Noem as Homeland Security Secretary following her disastrous performance at her congressional hearings in March, while Attorney General Pam Bondi was removed from her post a couple of months after a chaotic appearance at February hearings.

The UK must take more risks to “stay ahead of our enemies” as Russian incursions into British waters soar, the head of the Royal Navy has warned.

In a speech in central London, First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins said that Russian ship sightings have “jumped” by a third in two years and the UK was forced to respond dozens of times last year alone.

In response, he warned the UK had to invest not only in “the technologies of the future” but also have an “entire mindset” shift.

“If we are to stay ahead of our enemies, that requires us to take more risk, to ruthlessly remove unnecessary regulations and other barriers holding us back, so that we can cut the time it takes between trialling new systems and putting them to sea,” he said.

He warned that “things will only accelerate from here. The pace of technological change will never again be as slow as it is today”.

And he said that recent events in the Middle East, where Donald Trump’s Iran war led to the blockage of the crucial Strait of Hormuz, had hit home that “the sea and our ability to control it is central to our prosperity, our resilience and our very survival”.

His call comes just weeks after former defence secretaries and Labour grandees threw their weight behind a former Nato secretary general who warned that the UK’s security was “in peril” as a result of the “corrosive complacency” of Sir Keir Starmer.

George Robertson, a former Labour defence secretary who was appointed by the prime minister to write the government’s Strategic Defence Review (SDR), also accused “non-military experts” in the Treasury of “vandalism” and claimed Sir Keir was unwilling “to make the necessary investment” in Britain’s defence.

Russian ship Yantar was spotted in UK waters in January 2025 and then again in November ( Royal Navy/PA )

The First Sea Lord also announced that the first Navy-wide wargame to test the potential of its new “hybrid” approach was held last month.

In his speech at the Royal United Services Institute defence think tank, Sir Gwyn said: “The wargame provided clear evidence that our hybrid approach will deliver a significant increase in war-fighting capability.

“Our hybrid Navy generated a substantial increase in combat mass as measured by weapons and sensors, whilst also providing added flexibility and tactical choice for commanders.

“Our missile capacity increased threefold to the level necessary to win a contest in the North Atlantic.

“Across all our key missions, be it deterrence, carrier strike groups, amphibious strike groups, or integrated air and missile defence, we saw our readiness to respond improve markedly.”

He also said he was determined to leave the Royal Navy “much stronger than the one I inherited”.

He said: “By the time I depart in 2029, I am determined that the Royal Navy will be much stronger than the one I inherited, a fleet fit for 21st-century warfighting.”

News.content:

Perched in a tower atop a hill, Matthew Douglas climbs a staircase and emerges from a hatch on the roof, where a heavy glass ball in a metal cradle has burned a thin streak into a strip of paper, recording the previous day's sunlight.

It’s part of a routine he and other weather observers at Blue Hill Observatory and Science Center, a weather station 15 miles (24 kilometers) south of Boston, have followed every day for the last 141 years. Using largely unchanged analog tools, they have built a continuous record of temperature, humidity, precipitation, wind and other measurements that can feed weather forecasts and scientific research.

“My routine is the same every day,” said chief weather observer Douglas, who has worked there since 1997, sporting a dark blue sweatshirt with the name of the observatory on the front. “The only thing that changes are the numbers and the weather itself.”

Blue Hill is the nation’s oldest continually operating weather observatory, according to executive director Alex Evans. Since 1885, staff and volunteers have relied on many of the same instruments, including mercury and alcohol thermometers, hygrometers that use human hair to measure moisture in the air, and that glass sphere on the roof tracking the hours of bright sunshine.

Keeping the same tools in the same place for nearly a century and a half, Douglas said, means that if they spot a change in weather patterns, they can be sure it’s real and not a result of new instruments measuring data differently than the old ones. Having a “tried and true database” as a reference is very important for climate research, he added.

___

EDITOR’S NOTE: This story is a collaboration between the MIT Graduate Program in Science Writing and The Associated Press.

___

As climate science has come under fire from the Trump administration, budget cuts and layoffs have swept through federal weather institutions since 2025. Blue Hill, as a private nonprofit, avoided much of this maelstrom. However, its continuing work is not a given. Funding opportunities are limited in this political environment, Evans said.

Blue Hill’s work, though seemingly outpaced by modern technology, serves not just to keep weather records, but also to connect ordinary people to climate science.

A continuous weather record in America makes climate change visible

Few weather observatories in the U.S. are as old as Blue Hill, and fewer still continue to collect data manually. Though similar methods are still used by networks of volunteers across the country that feed data to the National Weather Service, weather observatories — both private ones and those affiliated with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration — have adopted automated digital systems since at least the 1990s.

Blue Hill sends a daily summary of its observations to the National Weather Service, which chief scientist Michael Iacono said may contribute to weather forecasts in some circumstances, and monthly summaries to the National Centers for Environmental Information, where they can be distributed to climate researchers. Local television meteorologists also receive the daily summaries and may use the observations in their broadcasts in rare cases, he said.

Inside Blue Hill’s round tower, which stands three stories tall with castle-like notches at the top, two weather observers, Douglas and Amanda Joly, share an office filled with the results of their daily work. Boxes with sun cards line the walls, wind-speed charts drawn on EKG paper fill the cabinets and computers store the spreadsheets where Douglas and Joly meticulously record temperature and humidity.

Having records that stretch back over 100 years “is really unique,” said Chris Fiebrich, a meteorologist at the University of Oklahoma. This “dataset is golden,” he said, because climate change involves slow trends so “you can only see that clearly if you have measurements that go way back, from before we had satellites” and other modern equipment.

Blue Hill’s records show, for example, a 5-degree Fahrenheit (or about 2.8-degree Celsius) increase in the average annual temperature at the observatory since 1885, and that two local ponds remain frozen during winter nearly three weeks less than they did then.

Observers can also spot the impact of climate policies. Since the 1990s, Blue Hill has recorded an uptick in bright sunlight duration after it reached a low point in the 1980s. Because air pollutants like particulate matter interfere with sunlight, cleaner air means more sunshine, so this uptick can partly be traced back to the Clean Air Act — a federal law passed in 1970 and amended in 1990 to improve air quality by reducing emissions of pollutants.

A third of Americans believe climate scientists understand “not too well” or “not at all well” whether climate change is happening, according to a Pew Research Center survey from 2023. Trump called climate change “the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world” in a speech at the United Nations General Assembly last September, and has sought to undermine climate science.

At a time when “the word ‘climate’ is politically demonized in some circles,” said Alan Sealls, president of the American Meteorological Society, places like Blue Hill can be “a small part of many possible solutions” to make weather and climate science relatable to people, including children.

Blue Hill connects people to science

The road to Blue Hill Observatory is a winding asphalt track that weaves through forest and borders a ski lift; making the drive, one needs to carefully wend between hikers and dog walkers. At the peak, visitors can enjoy the westward view over the treetops or slip through an open arch into the observatory’s courtyard.

Annie Hayes, a local from Milton who visited Blue Hill in mid-March with her husband and two children, said that seeing how observers collect data builds deeper trust in the science, which otherwise can seem “a little bit of a mystery.”

The mercury barometers in the observers’ office — one of which the observatory believes to be the oldest such instrument in active daily use in the United States — are a case in point. “If somebody’s standing there seeing it while you’re explaining it to them … it becomes a little less scary,” said chief scientist Iacono.

Blue Hill’s barometers, which measure atmospheric pressure, consist of glass tubes and small containers of mercury — a shiny, silver-white liquid — housed in a wooden case on the wall. As air presses down on the exposed mercury, it is forced up the tubes, and how far it travels reflects changes in atmospheric pressure. This is where the pressure unit “inches of mercury” comes from.

Another instrument popular with visitors is the Campbell-Stokes recorder, used to measure hours of bright sunshine. Its glass sphere, mounted in a curved metal frame, acts as a magnifying lens, focusing sunlight onto a paper card and burning a streak along it as the sun moves through the sky.

As she pointed to the glass sphere on display in the history room, Amanda Joly, Blue Hill’s deputy chief observer, explained that this recorder, which dates back to 1898, was stolen in 1993 and later recovered. The upside of that burglary is that, while a modern duplicate does the job on the building’s roof, visitors are now free to interact with the old sphere — something kids love to do — and the observers don’t have to worry about it affecting the measurements.

Hayes’ family, which lives nearby, was checking out some rain gauges in the gift shop when facilities head Don McCasland told them about a new Blue Hill citizen science program, which will allow residents to collect and add weather data to a central database. The family plans to start using their rain gauge this summer.

It’s “a great way to involve the kids and get them excited,” said Hayes. “And who knows? Maybe they’ll find an interest and want to pursue it on their own, too.”
